findings.title: The counted whole becomes individual entries
findings.claim: The pericope lets an individual's arrival be heard at the end of an administered count: 19:84 restrains haste while numbering, 19:94 exhaustively counts everyone, and 19:95 distributes that whole into persons who come one by one on the named Resurrection Day. The record, pebble-counter, and separated-pearl images make the count tangible while keeping each person distinct within it.
findings.mechanism: The doubled count in 19:84 and 19:94 supplies an independent numerical trigger for the pebble image carried by the 19:94 census word; the focus's kulluhum and fardan then meet counting, an earlier written claim in 19:79, and the named day. The repeated count can also color the interval as a counted span, while the focus's individual state gives the ledger and pearl images a person-level endpoint.
findings.reader_payoff: Solitary arrival becomes more than absence of company: each person remains a distinct, recorded unit within a complete count whose process has a named horizon.
findings.containment: The wording in 19:79 records what the claimant says, not a person's name; the ledger is an analogy. No physical pebble or pearl is stated, and the count does not establish an exact duration or a property-right judgment. The ordinary sense of arriving individually remains intact.

epistemic.reason: The channel nomination is a first-pass synthesis rather than an adjudicated recurring system, but its count, writing, totality, and individual-arrival contacts are locally supplied. Tactile and ledger details are kept analogical.

findings.title: What the claimant expected to carry
findings.claim: The focus completes the earlier claimant's boast: he expected wealth and offspring, 19:80 says God inherits what he says, and that verse closes with the same arrival-alone formula later used of everyone in 19:95. What failed to travel is not only company; the promised extensions of self are not portable.
findings.mechanism: Wealth and offspring claimed in 19:77 meet the transfer of inheritance and the exact fardan reprise in 19:80; the focus repeats that arrival formula with universal scope. The transfer changes the focus's solitude into the endpoint of dispossession, then 19:95 generalizes it to all.
findings.reader_payoff: The individual appearance becomes the final scene after wealth and lineage have ceased to function as companions or credentials.
findings.containment: This is an attributed contextual inference. A live alternative is that 19:80 asserts divine inheritance while fardan in both verses remains generic solitude; the focus still plainly says each person arrives individually.

findings.title: Support that cannot be owned
findings.claim: The adopted gods meant to strengthen their worshippers turn into opponents, and 19:87 says intercession is not possessed except under a covenant with the Most Merciful. Against that sequence, fardan can carry a bounded sense of arriving without a proxy one owns or commands, while an authorized relation remains conceptually possible.
findings.mechanism: The intended reinforcement in 19:81 is reversed by opposition in 19:82; the ownership and intercession terms of 19:87 specify the proxy relation, and its covenant clause limits the denial. The focus's individual presentation returns through fardan, changing total isolation into lack of controllable support.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold individual accountability together with the passage's narrow covenant exception, instead of reading solitude as the erasure of every possible relation.
findings.containment: The direct sense of fardan as a person arriving alone remains. The contextual reading does not decide who qualifies for intercession, and the stricter physical-aloneness reading remains live with the covenant clause treated separately.

epistemic.reason: The supplied root/index trace agrees with 19:81, 19:82, and 19:87 surfaces; the no-owned-proxy inference is an attributed contextual reading, not supplied target morphology.

findings.reader_payoff: Aloneness at arrival can remain plain while the passage leaves room for relation to be bestowed rather than carried as possession.
findings.containment: This is an attributed temporal/relational inference. The next ayah may describe worldly affection rather than an event after the Resurrection, so no afterlife chronology or permanent social condition is asserted.

epistemic.reason: The exact 19:96 word-index/root trace is present and matches lean context; the temporal relation between the focus and next ayah remains uncertain.
